identification: (1) Gent's Longines Ultra-Chron automatic, c.1967-72, 36,000 bph high-beat (cal. 431 family), silvered sunburst dial with applied baton markers, date window at 3, winged hourglass logo, 'Ultra-Chron' with the high-beat waveform logo, steel round case (about 34-35mm), Ultra-Chron medallion caseback, on a worn brown fabric strap. Crystal heavily scratched (most of the marks look like they are on the crystal, not the dial). (2) Small ladies round gold-plated manual-wind watch, white dial with baton markers, maker name on dial too small to read, caseback engraved 'V.M. FARR', on a gold-tone mesh bracelet.

viewing_check: Wind the crown and shake: does it run and does the date change? Check whether the scratches are on the crystal (cheap fix) or the dial. Look at the case back reference inside if they will open it. Read the ladies watch dial maker under a loupe.
